checkpoints.description: Task 'gaps-closure' completed successfully.
[1/2] Publish the canonical verification algorithm and a conformance vector for third-party verifiers

impact_assessment.why: The website will reimplement certificate canonicalization and digest verification in JavaScript. Without a public, pinned specification and vector, the browser verifier could drift from the Python verifier or silently accept a different payload.
impact_assessment.benefits: Third parties get an exact algorithm and a known-answer vector; the website test and the Python test pin the same bytes; the register-based trust model stays unchanged.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: additive documentation and one vector file; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: no certificate or register changes; legal: the vector is explicitly not an issued certificate
impact_assessment.mitigation: Test the vector through compute_digest in the public package, label it as a conformance fixture, and keep the HMAC key out of both the document and the vector.

checkpoints.description: Task 'licensing-v4' completed successfully.
[1/2] Harden the public verifier against wrong-typed certificate fields and publish the matching check order

impact_assessment.why: The public package reads untrusted certificate JSON. Mixed-type projects or allowances, a list expiry or a string is_perpetual raised TypeError during canonicalization or dataclass construction instead of returning INVALID_FORMAT, while the website verifier returned INVALID_FORMAT, so the reference and the browser could disagree.
impact_assessment.benefits: Malformed certificates now return a structured INVALID_FORMAT with a reason, no input can crash the verifier, and the website and Python reference share one documented order.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: no change to valid format-2 certificates or the register; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: none; compatibility: a malformed certificate now has a defined status instead of an exception
impact_assessment.mitigation: Tests cover every wrong-typed field and a mixed project list; the verification spec lists type checks before canonicalization; run all package and website parity tests.

checkpoints.description: [2/2] Wrong-typed fields now return INVALID_FORMAT before canonicalization; 57 tests and 4/4 gates pass. checklists: passed

handoff.state: the website verifier follows the same order

checkpoints.description: Task 'licensing-v5' completed successfully.
[1/2] Align the Python verifier with the browser on license_type, missing projects and strict dates

impact_assessment.why: The website verifier and the public Python reference must agree byte for byte and status for status; an empty license_type, a missing projects list and a non-hyphenated expiry could return different results.
impact_assessment.benefits: Both verifiers reject an explicitly empty license_type, default missing projects to *, and require hyphenated dates; the conformance vector and tests cover the shared contract.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: no change for valid format-2 certificates; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: none; compatibility: a non-hyphenated expiry is now INVALID_FORMAT instead of being accepted
impact_assessment.mitigation: Pin each case in both Python and Node suites, update the public verification order, and run both gates.
